item.title: China sets 17 per cent carbon intensity cut in new five-year climate plan
item.description: Beijing leans on rapid renewable expansion but sets no target for emissions decline before 2030.

item.title: The new age of resource competition needs transparency
item.description: As countries scramble to secure the minerals needed for clean energy, digital technologies, AI, and defense industries, the new era of resource competition implies both great promise and grave peril.

item.title: Malaysia urged to tighten financial rules to protect forests, communities
item.description: Findings from a new report reveal that current regulatory frameworks fall short of meeting the assessment criteria for financial regulation of global biodiversity targets.

item.title: Seafood fraud: There might be something fishy about your flounder
item.description: Seafood is so vulnerable to fraud that one in five products may not be what is claimed, warns the UNFAO.

item.title: Regulators invite feedback for new Malaysia sustainable finance taxonomy
item.description: The propsoed document will unify the central bank and securities commission’s existing taxonomies, as well as align the national sustaianble finance taxonomy with Asean's.

item.title: Philippines mandates storage for new utility scale renewable energy plants
item.description: The move could result in more expensive and fragmented storage units, warns industry association.

item.title: South Korea proposes revised rules to curb excessive courier packaging
item.description: The environment ministry has opened a public consultation on revised standards as a civic group reported widespread cases of excessive delivery packaging.

item.title: As the Gulf conflict widens, so does its environmental footprint
item.description: Environmental strain is growing in a region already vulnerable, leaving some countries with little capacity to cope.

item.title: The war in Iran could create a fertiliser shock, risking global food prices and farming
item.description: Around a third of globally traded urea passes through the Strait of Hormuz and importing countries are less self-sufficient than they appear.

item.title: Bangkok opens over 250 cooling centres as extreme heat grips Thai capital
item.description: Authorities in Thailand's capital have opened hundreds of temporary cooling shelters as scorching temperatures grip the city, warning that the heat index could reach levels considered dangerous for human health.
